name: Malarky
summary: Party bluffing game where players invent fake answers to everyday mysteries and vote for the true explanation.
rules_text: Players agree on number of rounds. Each round a host rolls a die and reads an Imponderable question from a card without seeing the answer, then shuffles concealed folders: one holds the true answer, others hold bluff instructions. Folders are dealt randomly, giving one secret truth-holder. After thinking time, players clockwise present answers in their own words, no exact repeats; duplicates must invent a backup bluff or be disqualified by vote. If the truth-holder hears the true answer before their turn they must bluff, called a forced Malarky. Then all vote secretly with colored chips for who they think told the truth, black chip if they held truth, empty hand if they claim to know truth on a bluff card. Scoring: +1 per vote received, +1 for voting for truth, +2 per vote if forced Malarky succeeds, -2 for wrong empty-hand guess.
rating_reason: Bluffing trivia with bluff cards and voting chips.
